facts.fact: National Treasury's circular says every municipality's property-rates billing report holds, per property, market value, category, amount billed, a unique property identifier linked to the valuation roll, owner and rebate, exemption and reduction values, because all financial systems use the valuation roll as the basis; it gives no count of municipalities.

The circular has each municipality reconcile its valuation roll (Part A register) to its own billing system and send the reconciliation, not the billing record, to National Treasury quarterly through the GoMuni upload portal, within 10 working days of quarter end.

systems.platform: various municipal financial systems from service providers
systems.tiers: municipalities (local government billing of property rates)

systems.system: GoMuni / Local Government Database and Reporting System (LGDRS)
systems.tiers: municipalities submit monthly mSCOA data strings, budgets and valuation-roll reconciliations
all municipalities must prepare budgets and the A1 schedule in their ERP
